'''''Smilax azorica''''' is a species of [[Flowering plant|flowering plants]] of the [[Smilacaceae]] family. The species is endemic to the [[Azores]]. It was first described in 1844 as ''Smilax divaricata'', a name that had already been given to another species. It was renamed ''Smilax azorica'' in 2009.<ref name=schaefer>Schaefer H., & Schoenfelder P. (2009). "[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233985485_Smilax_canariensis_S_azorica_Smilacaceae_and_the_genus_Smilaxin_Europe Smilax canariensis, S. azorica (Smilacaceae) and the genus Smilax in Europe.]" in ''Homenaje al Profesor Dr. Wolfredo Wildpret de la Torre''. Instituto de Estudios Canarios:  pp. 297-307.</ref>

==Description==
The species is a [[Vine|climbing wintergreen plant]]. It has few or no thorns. Its leaves are ovate or cordate, almost as broad as long. The flowers are unisexual, in a simple [[umbel]]. Its fruits are red when ripe.<ref name=schaefer/>
